## Overview

Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Implementation Patterns

### Bounded Queues with Blocking

The producer writes items to a bounded queue. Once the queue reaches capacity, the producer blocks (halts) until the consumer drains items and frees up space. This approach is straightforward but can cause the producer to stall completely if the consumer is slow.

### Credit-Based Flow Control

The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items (credits). The producer tracks available credits and stops sending once credits are exhausted. The consumer replenishes credits as it processes items. This gives finer control over the emission rate and avoids complete stalls.

### Reactive-Pull Models

Instead of the producer pushing items to the consumer, the consumer requests items on its own schedule. The producer only generates items in response to explicit pull requests. This inverts control: the consumer drives the pace entirely.

## Purpose

Backpressure prevents:
- Unbounded buffer growth
- Out-of-memory errors
- Cascading failures in multi-stage pipelines

By signaling the producer to slow down, backpressure ensures the entire pipeline operates at a stable, sustainable rate determined by the slowest stage.
